headline: Highest risk is medium: shared editor/repo context can leak or cascade code changes, while prompt-injection and compliance risks remain bounded by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot ingests editor buffers and repo context, and PaddleOCR can process documents/images, so a manual copy-paste or file-based bridge could carry malicious instructions. However, no shared clipboard/MCP channel is documented, and Copilot’s self-isolation plus human-review Workspace edits limit direct hijack. The pathway is plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF the operator copies PaddleOCR output into Copilot chat or open buffers
IF PaddleOCR processes attacker-controlled document text that is then pasted into Copilot
mitigations: Keep PaddleOCR output in a separate file from Copilot buffers
Require manual review before pasting any OCR text into Copilot
Strip instruction-like text from OCR outputs before reuse
Use a read-only handoff file for extracted text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to OCR outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open buffers, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images; if the same workspace contains sensitive documents, both agents can touch the same data class. Copilot’s vendor-only egress and PaddleOCR’s allowlisted egress reduce but do not eliminate leakage because the shared workspace itself is the exposure path. This is a default-configuration risk when both are used on the same files.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are opened in the same workspace used by Copilot
IF PaddleOCR extracts text from files that Copilot can read in repo context
mitigations: Separate sensitive documents from the coding workspace
Disable Copilot on folders containing OCR inputs/outputs
Review and redact OCR outputs before saving them into shared directories
Use distinct OS accounts or workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while PaddleOCR can run browsers and make allowlisted network calls. Even without explicit write access in PaddleOCR, the pair can still conflict through shared mutable files or generated artifacts in the same workspace. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so overlapping edits are plausible in default use.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR writes extracted artifacts into a directory Copilot also edits
IF Copilot applies Workspace edits while PaddleOCR-derived files are being regenerated
mitigations: Use separate output directories for OCR artifacts and code edits
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Commit or snapshot the repo before running either agent
Review diffs before accepting Copilot Workspace edits
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code or edits from repo context, and PaddleOCR can produce extracted text from documents/images that may be treated as authoritative input. If OCR errors or adversarial document content flow into Copilot without verification, the second agent can propagate them into code or documentation. The profiles show no built-in verification bridge, so the cascade is plausible.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is pasted into Copilot as trusted source text
IF Copilot Workspace edits are accepted without checking OCR provenance
mitigations: Verify OCR output against the source document before reuse
Mark OCR text as untrusted in filenames or comments
Require human review of Copilot-generated changes
Keep extracted text separate from code-generation prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between OCR and coding tools

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context, while PaddleOCR is open-source and locally described as document-processing. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different handling models and retention surfaces, so compliance gaps are possible if regulated documents are routed through Copilot. Only Copilot is cited because the issue is its vendor handling of repo context.
conditions: IF regulated documents or PII are placed into Copilot repo context
IF organizational policy forbids vendor processing of those documents
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of Copilot context
Use PaddleOCR only on approved local data
Review vendor data-processing terms before use
Redact PII before OCR and coding workflows
requires-engineering: route regulated data through a compliant environment
